text:
The candidate hypothesis proposes developing a specific dual-functional biosensor platform using a thermosensitive, pH-responsive P(NIPAM-co-BMA-co-NHSMA) hydrogel encapsulated with CD63 aptamers, operating at pH 6.5–7.5 and 30°C–37°C, with real-time characterization via surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) and fluorescence.

The provided abstract does not support this hypothesis. The study is a literature review that outlines the strengths and limitations of conventional and novel (microfluidic) EV isolation strategies, presents commercially available exosome isolation techniques and kits, and assesses the global market demand for exosome assays. It makes no mention of hydrogels, P(NIPAM-co-BMA-co-NHSMA), CD63 aptamers, SERS, fluorescence, or developing a biosensor platform.

VERDICT: REJECT
